scope: Remove obsolete ad-hoc timing and unused private diagnostic C entries while retaining functional kernel checks.

implementation.smp: Remove sequential_ns, parallel_ns and speedup_milli plus the unfair 1.050x pass threshold. Retain computed work equality, exact online/observed CPU masks, placement, monotonic-clock failures, bounded worker deadlines and all IRQ/TLB/lock/owner checks.
implementation.heap: Remove uncalibrated RDTSC timing and alloc_avg/free_avg/churn time output. Keep allocation, alignment, data patterns, double-free rejection, 2000-op churn, cleanup and live-byte/block balance. Existing SMP heap retention/poison probe is unchanged.
implementation.retained_helpers: Keep internal functions, live public R4DEV/Spectra contracts, useful isolated failure variants and USB self-tests needed by 0.84.16. SerialLink removal remains 0.84.34. Empty Kernel/Tests directories removed; no live test inventory entry deleted.
implementation.tcp: Remove only the separate optional boot TCP-burst call. Existing CHECK NETWORK LIMIT retains the privileged contract helper and its ten current cases.
implementation.quick: From the rebuilt canonical Test plan, derive a private Quick image with a standalone terminal, minimal AUTOEXEC and explicit CHECK NETWORK LIMIT. Kernel SMP probes stay enabled. Reject a stale canonical or private BOOT ELF. Require successful Spectra output and ERRORLEVEL within QUICKCHECK before the bounded QUICKPROBE stop.
implementation.marker_consumers: Update existing clock/general SMP parsers and synthetic fixtures together: validate matching CPU masks, BSP membership and CPU count; retain functional negative cases. Normal STANDARD source and method stay unchanged.

comparison_previous_release.observation: Overall decreases 5.80%, memory 11.50% and IPC 19.23%; scheduler increases 6.34%. This noticeable single-run difference is retained. Workloads, execution/storage/cache/clock context and comparison key match; Spectra/STDCHILD are byte-identical. Removed kernel test work is optional and disabled in STANDARD. No causal attribution, method change or extra run to improve the score.

performance_assessment: Normal kernel artifact and optional boot instrumentation change. Exactly one final Suite-2 STANDARD on SMP4 is required; already linker-discarded wrappers imply no claimed runtime gain.
limits: The 2000-op invasive HeapCheck keeps its original assertions but is not executed by the normal Quick configuration; the separate SMP HEAPPROBE is executed.
Parser self-tests are synthetic fixtures, including an existing failed-AP mask configuration; no extra guest failure-injection campaign is implied.
Only affected checks are run. No full catalog, browser campaign, physical hardware or Windows host claim.
One STANDARD is a descriptive single-run observation, not a causal performance estimate.
Full real benchmark exports and raw samples remain outside Git.
